03.06.2025, The Court On 10.06.2025 Passed The Following:

The petitioner is the accused in S.C.No.6/2024 on the files of the Additional District and Sessions Court (POCSO Act cases), Kozhikode, which arose out of Crime No.481/2021 of Medical College Police Station, Kozhikode.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Court (POCSO Act cases), Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The offence alleged against him is under Section 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The prosecution case is that on 17.02.2021, at about 4:30 p.m., he committed rape of a housewife having husband and child, inside a car parked at a lonely place.

It is stated that the survivor was in love with the accused consequent to their acquaintance, which commenced from the online platform 'sharechat', and that the accused gave the false promise of marriage to the survivor to win over her.

2. In the present petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the petitioner would contend that the offence alleged against the petitioner by the prosecution, is prima facie not made out from the allegations levelled against him.
It is further contended that the consensual sexual relationship between the petitioner and the survivor will not constitute the offence of rape.

Another reason stated by the petitioner for the quashment of the case against him is that the 2025:KER:39881 survivor has filed an affidavit before this Court stating that her relationship with the petitioner was purely consensual, and that she happened to prefer a complaint of rape against him due to some misunderstanding and ili- advice by her friends and relatives.

3.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

4. The survivor has filed an affidavit before this Court stating that her relationship with the petitioner was purely consensual, and that she had preferred the complaint against the petitioner due to some misunderstanding.
She further stated in the affidavit that she has no subsisting grievance against the petitioner, and that she is not interested in continuing the prosecution against the petitioner.
5. As already stated above, even by the prosecution case, the petitioner indulged in sexual intercourse with the survivor after winning over her by giving the promise of marriage.
It is not possible to say that the survivor happened to extend consent to the petitioner to have coitus with her on the basis of some misconception or false promise given by the petitioner.

This is because of the reason that the survivor, who is a housewife having husband and child, cannot be expected to have blindly 2025:KER:39881 believed the offer of the petitioner for marriage, since it was impossible to have such a marriage without her being divorced from the subsisting marital relationship with another person.

Thus, it is apparent from the facts and circumstances of the case that the survivor had consented for the sexual relationship with the petitioner on the day when she is said to have gone along with him in his car to the place where they resorted to sex inside the car.
The affidavit which the survivor has now filed before this Court also makes it clear that she had voluntary sexual relationship with the petitioner.
In that view of the matter, it cannot be said that the offence of rape is attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Needless to say that the prayer of the petitioner to quash the proceedings against him, has to be allowed.
